timing: After submission, before inspecting any pretrained baseline or fit outcomes; source and protocol were frozen before submission
expectation: Random supports may learn many targets at this broad all-layer budget. There is no established reason to expect guided pairing to win.
interpretation_rules: Paired transfer/preservation gains over all controls at comparable count would justify fresh testing, not a neuron-concept or novelty claim.
If outgoing-only trains as well as paired, the frozen co-trained ablation did not establish that incoming updates were required during fitting.
If every family reaches a ceiling, there is no demonstrated selection advantage; measure an honest budget/data frontier rather than changing this trial.
If LoRA wins, treat low-rank parameterization as the stronger baseline; do not infer a sparse advantage from storage counts alone.
Separate desired-answer-token likelihood from EOS likelihood in post-hoc analysis. Better stopping alone is not better counterfactual retrieval.
Any correction result must be considered with complete unrelated answers, aliases and label ambiguities. Literal target absence alone is insufficient.
postprocessing_note: After submission, the independent verifier was tightened to bind inputs.json bytes to the frozen protocol hash. No worker, data, loss, rates, supports, generation or scoring rules changed.
